papers.title: Redrock: Spectroscopic Classification and Redshift Fitting for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
papers.abstract: Redrock is a software package for spectroscopic classification and redshift fitting, designed to use the full information from spectroperfectionism outputs: flux-calibrated spectra, uncorrelated errors, and a per-spectrum resolution matrix encoding the non-Gaussian wavelength-dependent spectral line-spread function. Redrock was originally developed for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), but the Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS) also used Redrock as their primary galaxy redshift fitter prior to DESI. This paper presents the algorithmic details of Redrock and its performance on DESI data. On spectra from DESI DR2, Redrock achieves a redshift recovery rate of approximately 98% for the Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) and Luminous Red Galaxies (LRG), 95.9% for Emission Line Galaxies (ELG), and 92.6% for quasars (QSO), and it delivers unbiased stellar radial velocities with a precision of roughly 5 km/s.

papers.title: Mining the time axis with TRON. IV. MeerKAT detects a radio burst from a nearby M~dwarf
papers.abstract: We report the detection of a minute-timescale, highly circularly polarised ($\sim100\%$) radio burst from an active M dwarf (spectral type M1Ve), PM J14111$-$6155, located 19.6 pc from the Sun. Identified in the 1.28 GHz SMGPS using 8-second integrations from the TRON-pipeline, the burst peaked at 7.7 mJy. Visibility-based dynamic spectra reveal a drifting, band-limited emission feature ($\sim$300 MHz FWHM) with a maximum cut-off near 1.65 GHz, associated with electron cyclotron maser instability (ECMI), implying the existence of large-scale magnetic topologies ($B_* \approx 0.59$ kG). A non-detection ($3\sigma$ upper limit) four hours later points to intermittent or rotationally modulated beamed emission. An analysis of both TESS and ground-based survey data failed to recover an unambiguous rotational period for the optical counterpart. Follow-up SALT spectroscopy confirms its active chromospheric state, exhibiting prominent emission in the Ca {\sc ii} infrared triplet, Balmer lines, and persistent double-peaked H$\alpha$ emission ($44.6\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ peak separation) attributable to optically thick self-absorption. This discovery demonstrates that the coordinated use of time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enables direct probing of coherent radio emission from the magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs.

papers.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
papers.abstract: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars. This is theorized to happen via Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here, we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, that originates from the CEE of a ~7M$_{\odot}$ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as a ~0.7M$_{\odot}$ companion inspiraling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven year period of gradual brightening - the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core within a few (<10) orbits powers the ejection of the outermost ~10% of the stellar envelope at speeds ~10x the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope, $0.01\lesssim \alpha \lesssim 0.4$. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

papers.title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
papers.abstract: The central star of Pa30 and its nebulosity offer one of the best opportunities to study a SN Iax explosion and its remnant. Pa30 is thought to be the product of the historical supernova explosion of 1181. No infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star has hitherto been reported. Here, we present a 0.75-5 $\mu$m spectrum taken by the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), together with ground-based infrared spectra, at higher resolution, covering the 0.8-2.5 $\mu$m region. The spectra contain very broad lines, which we have attempted to identify and model using the codes CMFGEN and CLOUDY. The CMFGEN modelling suggests that most of the lines are due to OVI. However, CLOUDY modelling, using expected theoretical abundances for the bound remnants of SN Iax explosions, provides evidence for the presence of coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from a shocked gas. This strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

papers.title: Asteroseismology of AI Velorum: a prototype of high-amplitude delta Scuti stars
papers.abstract: AI Velorum is exceptional among high-amplitude \delta Scuti (HADS) stars because of its multimode pulsations. Despite being an excellent target for asteroseismology, this prototype star has not been studied in detail. We determine the stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of AI Vel, constrain envelope convection and convective core overshooting, and test three opacity data sets: OPAL, OP, and OPLIB. We analysed TESS photometry, ground-based Str\"omgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy. Modes were identified using photometric and spectroscopic methods, and empirical values of the non-adiabatic f-parameter were derived for both radial modes. Seismic modelling was performed within a Bayesian framework supported by Monte Carlo simulations. We confirm the radial nature of the two dominant modes and identify one non-radial mode as most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Within the explored parameter space, only OPAL models reproduce the observed position of AI Vel in the HR diagram, whereas OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favour inefficient envelope convection (mixing-length parameter alpha_{mlt}\lesssim 0.5). Including the non-radial mode substantially reduces the formal posterior uncertainties, but the ambiguity in its identification introduces additional model-dependent uncertainties. AI Vel is an evolved, slowly rotating star in the hydrogen shell-burning phase. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters. The preference for OPAL opacities is consistent with results for several other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply a general superiority of OPAL opacities.

papers.title: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns). For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%. Retrievals of combined NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations yield consistent atmospheric properties. For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03). Divergence metrics, Wasserstein distances, posterior overlaps, and coverage tests assess posterior fidelity and uncertainty calibration, revealing parameter-dependent differences. Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.

papers.title: Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with mass estimates verifiable in Gaia Data Release 4
papers.abstract: Gaia Science Alerts provide an all-sky stream of photometric transients, including events consistent with gravitational microlensing. For such events, forthcoming epoch astrometry from the Gaia mission offers the possibility of testing photometric lens mass predictions. While microlensing parallax inferred from the photometric light curve can constrain the event geometry, a direct lens mass measurement additionally requires the angular Einstein radius, which may be accessible through astrometric microlensing. We aim to construct a pre-Data-Release-4 (DR4) sample of Gaia microlensing events for which the available photometry provides a measurable microlensing-parallax signal. This allows us to derive statistical predictions for the lens mass and distance. We forward-modelled these events to predict the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal in Gaia DR4. We identify 56 Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with 71 point-source point-lens solutions with annual parallaxes that satisfy our fit-quality, posterior-boundedness, and parallax-significance criteria. Lens masses and distances were inferred using two prior-based frameworks, pyLIMASS and the Besan\c{c}on Galaxy Model, which combine the measured microlensing parameters and Gaia source information with stellar-population and Galactic models. These inferred parameters were used to simulate Gaia DR4-like along-scan astrometry and estimate the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal. The inferred lens masses and distances remain strongly prior-dependent without a direct angular Einstein radius measurement. Among the 284 event-solution-prior branches, 47 are classified as high-confidence astrometric detections using Gaia DR4-like simulations. These predictions can be tested once epoch astrometry is released in Gaia DR4.

papers.title: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
papers.abstract: Stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) originate from massive progenitors that have lost most or all of their outer envelopes prior to core collapse. Recent advances in optical time-domain surveys have revealed a growing population of peculiar SESNe with unusual light-curve morphologies, pointing to energy sources beyond the standard radioactive-decay scenario. In this work, we present multi-band photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a peculiar Type Ib supernova discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). SN 2025wiu is characterized by a high luminosity and exceptionally slow photometric evolution, with a prominent post-maximum bump peaking at $\sim50$ days after the primary maximum. Its early light curve also shows a weak excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a compact progenitor with a radius of $\sim4\,R_\odot$. The spectra show only modest evolution, with persistently weak line features and no narrow emission lines detected even at $\sim110$ days after maximum. By modeling the primary peak and late-time tail with a combination of radioactive decay and additional energy sources, we isolate the post-maximum bump, which has a roughly symmetric profile with a peak luminosity of $\sim2.4 \times 10^{42}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and a characteristic duration of $\sim42$ days. We discuss circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, accretion, magnetar activity, and a double $^{56}$Ni distribution as possible origins of the bump. The latter three scenarios face challenges in reproducing the post-maximum bump, while delayed CSM interaction remains a possible explanation.

papers.title: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
papers.abstract: We present ARTIS radiative transfer calculations for neutron star merger ejecta with line-by-line opacities, wavelength-calibrated lanthanide data, and time-dependent r-process compositions and thermalisation, testing how the early kilonova depends on the mass-velocity distribution, dimensionality, and line treatment. We rescale 3D dynamical ejecta from a merger simulation in density and velocity to approximate AT2017gfo. Mass scaling alone provides good agreement with the bolometric light curve but inconsistent spectra. With velocities additionally halved, the model also reproduces the observed spectra at 1.4, 2.4, and (albeit less accurately) 3.4 days. The Sr II triplet contributes most to the 10500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ peak, and La III and Gd III to the 13500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ shoulder. Although hydrodynamically not fully self-consistent, this model is to our knowledge the first kilonova model based on calibrated atomic data that reproduces the light curve and main spectral features of the early AT2017gfo, suggesting that total (dynamical plus post-merger) ejecta with higher mass, lower velocity, and similar composition compared to our dynamical ejecta could explain AT2017gfo. A 2D azimuthal average mixes lanthanide-poor with lanthanide-rich regions, smooths the density, and makes the averaged model three times fainter at 1 day and redder throughout than the 3D model, highlighting the importance of 3D modelling. We compare the line-by-line macroatom treatment with expansion-opacity and line-binned schemes with thermal redistribution, using identical atomic data. Luminosities agree to $\lesssim 10$ per cent after 1 day, but the expansion-opacity scheme, unlike converged line-binned schemes, overestimates the spectral flux by up to 20 per cent, which can bias inferred abundances.

papers.title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
papers.abstract: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.

papers.title: The Science and Technology of Broad-Band X-ray Astrophysics
papers.abstract: Much of our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena over the past decade has relied on coordinated observations extending from soft X-rays (<10 keV) to hard X-rays (>10 keV). While soft X-ray facilities remain abundant, focusing capabilities above ~10 keV are scarce, representing the primary gap for broad-band X-ray science. Simultaneous wide-band observations are essential to study thermal and non-thermal processes in extreme environments such as accretion discs, jets, and coronae. However, current high-energy observations remain limited by a lack of high angular resolution and sensitivity beyond Chandra's bandpass. With upcoming multi-messenger facilities set to dramatically increase variable and transient sources, a high angular resolution broad-band X-ray mission is critically needed. This report reviews the current landscape of high-energy facilities, outlines key science drivers, focusing on extragalactic accretion (the cosmic X-ray background) and Galactic compact objects, and examines the underlying technology landscape, including optics and detectors. Broad-band X-ray astrophysics is primed to address key questions from the Astro2020 Decadal Survey. While past focusing efforts have been limited to the Small Explorer class, technological advances now enable low-risk Probe- or Flagship-class architectures capable of delivering order-of-magnitude improvements in capabilities.

papers.title: A higher-order smoothness indicator as refinement criterion for Newtonian and relativistic MHD simulations
papers.abstract: Adaptive mesh refinement is a widely adopted strategy for grid-based numerical simulation codes to mitigate the high computational cost of multi-length scale problems. A robust and reliable mesh refinement criterion with minimal requirement for problem-specific tuning is critical for efficient and accurate simulations. Motivated by the oscillation indicators used in the spectral methods literature, we develop a new mesh refinement criterion employing a 5-point stencil for multi-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics simulations, essentially extending the conventional 3-point L\"ohner scheme. We implement the criterion in the astrophysical fluid dynamics code AthenaK and test it across a variety of benchmark problems in Newtonian, special relativistic, and general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, demonstrating its robustness and versatility.

papers.title: Computation of complex dust grain optical properties: Optimisation method by equivalent representation (OMER)
papers.abstract: Computing the optical properties of dust grains is important for understanding various astrophysical environments. However, the numerical methods used to compute these properties require significant computing resources for irregularly shaped or inhomogeneous particles that are representative of realistic grown dust. This study aims to provide an efficient yet accurate Discrete dipole approximation (DDA) computation method for large aggregates with 'complex' monomers and structural details or compositional inhomogeneities. We propose the optimisation method by equivalent representation (OMER) method, which uses optimisation of the optical properties of a known monomer to find an equivalent homogeneous sphere. This sphere can then be used as a substitute for the complex monomer in large aggregates. The method provides a good approximation of complex monomers, as demonstrated in test cases involving large aggregates. Compared to existing methods, OMER shows greater accuracy, particularly in the range from visible to submillimetre wavelengths. The gain in computing time depends on the grain but can exceed two orders of magnitude. The proposed method provides a fast and accurate approximation for estimating the optical properties of materials with complex shapes and paves the way for efficient computation cross-sections for complex dust grain aggregates with thin core-mantle structures or hierarchical aggregates of large sizes.

papers.title: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
papers.abstract: With the fourth data release (DR4) from Gaia imminent, we predict neutron star (NS) binaries with luminous companions (LCs) expected to be detectable in DR4 and the final data release (DR5). We create realistic synthetic populations of NS--LC binaries in the Milky Way using COSMIC, assuming (a) observationally motivated initial distributions of binary properties, (b) metallicity and location dependent star formation history of the MW adopted from the FIRE-2 galaxy m12i, and (c) all relevant binary interaction physics, with the rapid and delayed supernova prescriptions. We estimate the detectable NS--LC population using an approximate Gaia\ selection function based on projected orbital size of the LC as well as gaiamock, which emulates Gaia's multi-epoch astrometry and orbit-fitting pipeline- both after taking into account extinction and reddening. Across supernova models and statistical fluctuations, the former (gaiamock) pipeline predicts $\sim14$--$29$ ($\sim1$--$8$), $4500$--$4700$ ($100$--$110$), and $4800$--$5000$ ($300$--$380$) detectable NS--LC binaries in DR3, DR4, and DR5, respectively. While the orbital-size based pipeline brackets the DR3 yield of NS--LC candidates, the gaiamock prediction falls short, suggesting uncertainties in the modeled binary evolution or contributions from other formation channels. DR4 is expected to directly shed light on the the relative importance of detectable NS--LC binaries from isolated binary evolution vis a vis other channels such as dynamical formation. Interestingly, our models suggest that future releases will also include $22^{+7}_{-5}\ (13^{+5}_{-4})$ and $124^{+14}_{-15}\ (53^{+10}_{-6})$ gaiamock-detectable pulsar--MS binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively, for the rapid (delayed) model, which are prime targets for radio follow-up.

papers.title: Maximising the Open Magnetic Flux of a Star
papers.abstract: We consider how to distribute the magnetic flux on a star's surface in order to maximise the proportion of open magnetic flux predicted by the potential field source surface model. The proportion of open flux is shown to be maximised by concentrating all of the positive and negative flux at antipodal points. For a typical source surface height, this enhances the open flux by 35% compared to a dipolar distribution. Even if the flux is spread over finite polar caps -- as on the Sun around Solar Minimum -- the open flux is still substantially enhanced compared to the dipole. Nevertheless, we show that the dipole approximation over-estimates the open flux for this kind of flux distribution.

papers.title: Multifrequency deep radio continuum VLA observations toward OMC-2/3
papers.abstract: We present multiwavelength (0.7-5 cm) Very Large Array continuum observations of high sensitivity (3 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$), reaching an angular resolution of $0.4''$ (154 au) toward the Integral Shaped Filament in Orion. We image a field of $12.5'$ in diameter, containing the whole OMC-2 region and the southernmost $2.5'$ of OMC-3. We report the positions, flux densities and spectral indices of 47 radio sources, and discuss their nature. We conclude that, out of the 57 radio sources in the field of view, 36 (63%) are very likely tracing YSOs, 4 are tracing jet/outflow knots, and 6 are extragalactic sources; the nature of the remaining sources is unclear. We identify the driving sources of the 9 previously reported molecular outflows in our field of view. Four of them show a clear elongated radio jet morphology. We detect free-free emission from two potential photoevaporating discs associated with Class III YSOs. We find variability in 11 radio sources, 7 of which are also variable at shorter wavelengths. We find 7 pairs of radio sources with projected separations of 150-3000 au, which are potential binary systems; we identify a total of 17 potential multiple systems within this separation range when taking into account sources detected at other wavelengths. This work highlights the potential of deep VLA observations to uncover a large population of weak radio sources and study their diversity, serving as a guide for future surveys with the SKA and ngVLA.

papers.title: Sun-like stars show lowered X-ray activity together with over-rotation at beyond-solar ages
papers.abstract: In recent years, substructure in the age-rotation relationship of cool, sun-like stars has been identified, showing deviations from the historical Skumanich law. Since magnetic activity is expected to be the physical root cause of the stellar spin-down, namely via the magnetic braking process mediated through stellar winds, changes in spin-down should correspond to unusual activity behaviour. We selected a sample of old sun-like stars in the solar neighborhood with asteroseismic age estimates and measured rotation periods, and present an analysis of their magnetic activity using deep X-ray observations from XMM-Newton. We observe that sample stars less massive than the Sun (late-G and early-K) agree well with the established rotation-activity relationship, while early-G and late-F stars with masses above solar tend to be unusually X-ray dim for their rotation period. The latter stars rotate faster than same-colour stars in the solar-age open cluster M67, despite being older than M67. Those stars are characterized by either low metallicity ([Fe/H]$\approx -0.2$ dex compared to solar) or by a mix of low coronal temperatures ($< 1.5$ million K) and very low X-ray surface fluxes ($\lesssim 10^4$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$). We conclude that there is sufficient dynamo activity for coronal emission in the sample stars, since we successfully detect the majority of them in our X-ray observations. We argue that stars with extremely low coronal temperature and/or low X-ray flux through the stellar surface may produce an inefficient spin-down through hampered angular momentum shedding. If this is indeed the cause for their over-rotation, the onset age of this effect would need to be at an age of approximately 3~Gyr. However, this behaviour is at odds with studies of stars in the open cluster M67 with a cluster age of $\sim4$ Gyr, which do not show a faster-rotating population of sun-like stars.

papers.title: Welop\=o'ai: A peculiar triple system 8 pc from the Sun
papers.abstract: Context. We report the serendipitous discovery of a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) during a radial-velocity search for exoplanets with SPIRou. The system is located at 8.46 pc and forms a hierarchical triple with a more distant white dwarf, which has no known analogue within 30 pc. Aims. We characterise the orbital architecture and component masses through a joint Keplerian fit of radial velocities and astrometry, derive the physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs, and discuss the implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics. Methods. We obtained radial velocity measurements with SPIRou spread over 4.8 yr, revealing a large-amplitude signal ($\sim$16 km/s peak-to-peak) that is inconsistent with planetary companions. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and near-infrared (NIR) imaging with GNIRS confirmed a white dwarf companion at sub-arcsecond separation. Results. The system comprises an inner binary with a semi-major axis of $4.644 \pm 0.017$ au ($P \approx 9.83$ yr), consisting of the primary M4 V ($M = 0.4189^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072} M_\odot$) and a white dwarf companion ($M = 0.6180^{+0.0046}_{-0.0045} M_\odot$, $T_{\rm eff} \sim 5210 \pm 320$ K, cooling age 5.3-5.5 Gyr). This inner pair lies at a projected separation of 123.9 au ($P > 1000$ yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The dynamically determined mass of the inner white dwarf is one of only a handful of such measurements for white dwarfs within 20 pc, and the most precise, at the sub-percent (0.7%) level. Conclusions. This system is the closest known triple containing multiple white dwarfs and offers direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability. Furthermore, a tentative near-infrared (IR) excess towards the inner white dwarf further hints at circumstellar dust.

papers.title: Analytical formulae for planet-planet or moon-moon tides
papers.abstract: Almost negligible among the solar system planets, mutual tides raised by a secondary on another secondary orbiting the same primary may gain increased importance in tightly packed systems, e.g., between the components of close-in exoplanetary systems or between the moons of gas giants. In this work, we derive an analytical formula for the planet-planet tidal potential and for the effect of mutual tides on the rotational and orbital evolution of moons or planets in a coplanar configuration. The procedure follows closely the steps of W. M. Kaula (1961), and the resulting potential and derived quantities are presented in the form of an expansion into modes of different frequencies (in the temporal domain) and spherical harmonic components (in the spatial domain). The analytical formulae are implemented into a code and compared with an independent numerical solution.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
papers.abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire most of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock gas entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We aim to build a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic conditions, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term planetary interior evolution by training a physics-informed neural network (PINN) predictor on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This PINN provides post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. The PINN predicts higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with PINN-derived boundary conditions achieve intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2 R_{\mathrm{J}}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1 M_{\mathrm{J}}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

papers.title: Potential spectral markers of intrinsic magnetic fields of hot exoplanets in the UV range
papers.abstract: A method for detecting the intrinsic magnetic fields of exoplanets, based on the effect of atomic alignment (the redistribution of populations among magnetic sublevels under the action of anisotropic radiation from the host star), has been adapted for observations with the Spektr-UV space telescope. A procedure for selecting sensitive transitions is proposed, and triplet absorption lines in the UV range that are sensitive to alignment are identified. On the basis of three-dimensional aeronomic models of the hot Jupiters KELT-20 b and HAT-P-32 b, absorption spectra in these lines are calculated for cases with and without intrinsic magnetic fields of the exoplanets. Using the Spektr-UV exposure-time calculator, the observability of the effect is assessed, and an observing program is proposed, specifying the optimal duration of individual exposures and the number of transits required to detect the signal.

papers.title: A Homogeneous Benchmark of Exoplanet Mass-Radius Relations
papers.abstract: The mass-radius ($M$-$R$) relation is fundamental to inferring the bulk composition and internal structure of exoplanets. However, published relations remain difficult to compare directly because studies adopt different planetary samples, fitting procedures, and evaluation metrics. We construct a homogeneous, quality-controlled benchmark of 963 exoplanets with dynamically measured masses and transit radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. We compare empirical power laws, probabilistic models, and machine-learning (ML) regressors using point accuracy, interval coverage, and probabilistic calibration. On the full test set, a multi-feature random forest has the lowest root-mean-square error, 0.329~dex in $\log_{10} M$ versus 0.368~dex for a fitted two-parameter power law ($p = 0.007$ unadjusted; $p = 0.059$ after Holm correction across 13 comparisons). Radius-only ML models perform comparably to the single power law. In three ranges of the measured radius, several methods improve on the power law below 1.6 $R_\oplus$, but none does between 1.6 and 4 $R_\oplus$. Including stellar and orbital covariates significantly improves predictions only for low-mass planets ($M < 4.4\,M_\oplus$), although this result is sensitive to missing covariate data and weakens when the training and test sets are separated by host star. Within their calibrated radius domains, the published empirical and probabilistic relations remain highly competitive. Finally, a first-order variance decomposition shows that formal measurement uncertainties account for only $\sim$3\% of the residual variance (0.067 of 0.401~dex), and the remaining $\sim$0.396~dex arises from compositional diversity, selection effects, and model approximation error.

papers.title: Discovery of a Massive Outer Companion to the TOI-178 Resonant Chain
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of a massive outer companion around TOI-178, a known planetary system with six inner small planets within 0.15 AU, five of which are in a 2:4:6:9:12 resonant chain. We analyse the astrometric anomalies in the combined Gaia DR2/DR3 - Hipparcos catalogue (G23H) and literature radial velocities, revealing strong evidence for a massive outer companion at several AU. We combine the resulting orbital fit posterior with archival high-contrast imaging to constrain the properties of the corresponding massive outer companion, TOI-178 h. We also study the dynamical stability of the inner resonant chain in the presence of this previously unknown outer companion via both heuristic and N-body simulations. We find that the inner system appears to be robust to the perturbing influence of TOI-178\,h, in line with the systems several Gyr age. Our analysis results in a final posterior solution for TOI-178\,h with a semi-major axis of $6.9^{+12.3}_{-3.3}$ AU, a mass of $21^{+47}_{-11} M_J$, and eccentricity of $0.76^{+0.18}_{-0.35}$, likely corresponding to an eccentric brown dwarf. TOI-178 is currently the only known system that has maintained a high-multiplicity resonant chain whilst in the dynamical presence of a massive outer companion, showcasing a unique outcome of planet formation.

papers.title: Integrating AI Coding Agents Into Scientific Research
papers.abstract: New software tools have emerged that enable AI agents to quickly develop code that analyzes data and generates figures, but their mistakes can also harm a researcher's computer, require extensive resources for validation, and cause the results to be received more skeptically. These concerns could be mitigated if scientific software is developed in a secure environment with a system for monitoring file changes and well-defined standards for handling AI agents. This paper first describes how coding agents change eleven aspects of generating, verifying, and reproducing numerical results. A six-level scale is then proposed for classifying AI-assisted numerical experiments by their provenance, reproducibility, openness, oversight, and falsifiability (PROOF). The scale begins with locally self-consistent, version-controlled, human-verified results and culminates in a publicly accessible and curated archive of the files, change history, prompt transcripts, independent agent regeneration of the analysis, and multiple cryptographically verifiable attestations of regeneration by independent researchers. These aspects of AI-assisted scientific software development have been synthesized into a new open source software package called vaibify that optimizes the agentic development of computational experiments ascending the PROOF Ladder. Docker containers sequester the agents while a GUI enables researchers to prompt command line agents, monitor the current status of local and remote files, and drive a project to PROOF Level 3 (reproducible). The methods described in this paper could help researchers reduce the time required to verify agent-written software and efficiently communicate trust in AI-assisted science.

papers.title: Why supersonic UAP events are not accompanied by acoustic booms?
papers.abstract: The Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) events have been recorded for decades. However, the nature of these events remains unknown. We advocate an idea that the dark matter (DM) in form of the axion quark nuggets (AQN) made of standard model quarks (or {\it antiquarks}) and gluons could {\it simultaneously} explain many observed puzzling features which always accompany the UAP events, such as high velocity, enormous acceleration, absence of any remaining materials in affected area, etc. This long list of mysterious features also includes the absence of any sound which normally accompanies any supersonic motion. The AQN framework answers this last puzzle as well, which represents the title of the present work. The AQN dark matter model was invented long ago without any intension to apply the model to UAP events. Rather, it was invented with a single motivation to explain the observed similarity $\Omega_{\rm DM}\sim \Omega_{\rm visible}$ between visible and DM components, which represents a very generic feature of this framework, not sensitive to any parameters of the construction. In this work we use the same framework with the same set of parameters to study the observed UAP events. Essentially we argue that a specific class of UAP represents the close cousin of other mysteries known for decades (even centuries), such as sky-quakes, Ball Lightnings, and Mysterious Transient events. In other words, the UAPs represent different manifestations of exactly the same objects, the AQNs propagating in atmosphere. The fuel powering all these mysterious energetic events is one and the same: it is the antiquark core of the AQNs. We also present some suggestions on type of instruments required to study this specific (and well defined) type of the UAP events.

papers.title: Isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux limits from Carpet-3 experiment data using neural networks with domain adaptation
papers.abstract: Diffuse gamma rays above 100 TeV probe PeV cosmic rays and astrophysical neutrino sources. Their strong attenuation on background radiation makes the observed flux sensitive to the location of the emission and to possible modifications of photon propagation. Searches for an isotropic component require rejection of an overwhelming hadronic background, but uncertainties in air-shower physics, cosmic-ray composition and detector response can lead to differences between simulated and measured events. Here we report upper limits on the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux from 100 TeV to 10 PeV using 1078 days of Carpet-3 observations collected between 2022 and 2026. We identify photon candidates with a neural network combining the surface-array signals and measurements from the upgraded 410 $\mathrm{m^2}$ muon detector. Unsupervised domain adaptation uses unlabeled experimental events during training to mitigate the impact of simulation--data discrepancies on the classification. The limits are among the strongest available and provide benchmarks for tests of extended Galactic emission and modified photon propagation from extragalactic sources.

papers.title: JEPA for astronomy: multi-survey spectral alignment puts stellar parameters on the leading principal axes
papers.abstract: Spectra from different surveys carry different systematics and are not calibrated against one another. Multi-survey foundation models for stellar spectra are then built by aligning embeddings of the same star observed across surveys. Most in astronomy follow the recipes established for language and vision, aligning with a contrastive loss that separates every star from the others. However, this does not ensure that the stellar physics is encoded in a form that a simple read-out can recover. Holding the cross-survey architecture fixed and varying only the alignment loss, we measure what an objective encodes from the principal-component geometry of the Gaia BP/RP (XP) spectra and from a linear probe of the stellar parameters. In a properly aligned embedding, the leading two principal components form a plane that recovers an analog of the Kiel diagram, the third component tracks [Fe/H], and [alpha/Fe] varies coherently across the plane, such that the chemically defined Galactic disks and accreted populations occupy distinct loci. We show that legibility, the ease of reading the information out, is highest for a training objective that never pushes stars apart, and instead constrains only the overall distribution of each survey's embeddings (JEPA). JEPA also exceeds the contrastive alternative at the same architecture, and the performance improves further as more surveys (Gaia XP+LAMOST LRS+DESI+APOGEE) are included. Predicted abundances for 8.0 million XP giants reproduce the main [alpha/Fe]-[Fe/H] structure of the Milky Way. These results indicate that the choice of alignment objective, not alignment alone, determines whether stellar labels are linearly recoverable.

papers.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
papers.abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. We investigate whether the latter provides an adaptive alternative to FM-based scientific retrieval. We evaluate this approach on a galaxy retrieval task spanning diverse modalities--history of star formation, spectra of light emitted, and multi-wavelength observations from two telescopes--comparing an FM baseline with separately trained embeddings fused through multi-objective optimization based on Pareto optimality. We find that the FM baseline achieves strong embedding-space proximity, but our method preserves modality-specific distance structure that allows scientists to inspect which physical signals drive similarity. Our method also achieves improved fidelity in raw-data space: across six measured properties, its nearest neighbor is 8% closer to the query on average than that retrieved by kNN in the FM embedding space (spread 0.128 vs. 0.139). These results suggest that multi-objective retrieval can surface astrophysically coherent candidates that single-objective search alone may overlook.

papers.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
papers.abstract: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

papers.title: Subsequent Dust-Fading Events of the Wolf-Rayet Star WR 59: A Continuous Visual Record
papers.abstract: This paper presents long-term visual and space-based monitoring of the WC9d Wolf-Rayet star WR 59 from 2017 to 2026, documenting a profound physical transition from a stable baseline to an ongoing phase of continuous dust production. Visual observations using a 22-inch telescope initially established a four-year quiescent baseline at magnitude 13.9. Following the historic May 2021 discovery fade to magnitude 15.2, long-term nightly visual monitoring documented an accelerating sequence of twelve distinct fading episodes over subsequent years, characterised by progressively shorter inter-fade recovery intervals. Due to severe pixel crowding and flux contamination from a close 11.7 V companion star 11 arcseconds away, automated large-pixel survey pipelines remain completely blind to these high-amplitude fading events. Direct comparisons with NASA's TESS satellite photometry during quiet phases show that targeted visual magnitude estimates measure systemic baseline micro-variations with professional accuracy while bridging space mission coverage gaps. High-density observation blocks during the minimum floor reveal a highly dynamic, rapid, minute-by-minute bimodal oscillation and sub-minute flickering between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2. At the time of writing, the system remains locked in an unprecedented deep minimum, varying between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2 for a sustained period exceeding 102 consecutive days. Intensive visual monitoring is ongoing to record the eventual egress recovery profile.

papers.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the E\"otv\"os parameter is $\eta\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $\alpha\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $\lambda\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

papers.title: A Butterfly Collector's View of Fast Radio Bursts: Repeating Sources Go Quiet within a Few Years
papers.abstract: How long repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources stay active is key to their origins but poorly known as a population. We test this with unseen species estimation, a method first used to predict how many new butterfly species a further collecting trip would find. If each source keeps the same mean rate over time, the number of sources seen $k+1$ times in one window predicts how many bursts the sources seen $k$ times will emit in a later window. It assumes neither the burst rate distribution nor source distances. For the five years of CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure the ratio $R$ of observed to predicted bursts against the gap $\Delta$ between windows. A steady mean rate gives $R = 1$ at every $\Delta$, so a change of $R$ with $\Delta$ means that the sources change. $R$ is close to unity for $\Delta \lesssim 60$ days and drops by half within one year. Neither steady nor randomly fluctuating sources reproduce this decline, unless the latter are mostly silent. Three models explain the data equally well: a lifetime of about three years, on/off activity with two-year active phases, or a mix of short- and long-lived sources. Fitted to the first three years alone, they correctly predict the further decline of $R$ in the last two years. Longer monitoring of $R$, and of whether silent sources come back to life, will distinguish them. Unlike butterfly species, FRB sources do not wait for the next collecting trip, so follow-up should start soon.

papers.title: Calibration of LHAASO-WCDA Energy Scale using Cosmic Ray Moon Shadow
papers.abstract: Cosmic-ray particles in the TeV range, originating outside the solar system, are partially blocked on their way to Earth by the Moon, producing a deficit in their flux known as the Moon shadow. This work presents a precision measurement of the westward shift of the Moon's shadow using 3.4 years of data from LHAASO's Water Cherenkov Detector Array (WCDA). We use this direct physical measurement, combined with four cosmic-ray composition models, each divided into five mass groups, to calibrate the detector's absolute energy response in the range of 4 - 37 TeV. We quantify the fractional deviation between the calibrated and simulated energy scales by determining a best-fit scale shift parameter of $\epsilon$ =-0.04 $\pm$ 0.03. This yields a 95% confidence interval of -9% to +0.2% for the systematic energy scale deviation. Complementing the simulation based on hadronic interaction model, this geomagnetic calibration provides a data-driven physical validation of the simulated WCDA energy response, effectively bounding systematic uncertainties and refining the overall energy scale.

papers.title: Design and performance of the front-end readout electronics for LACT
papers.abstract: The Large Array of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (LACT) will complement the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) with a target angular resolution of 0.05 degrees to resolve the morphology of Very-High-Energy gamma-ray sources. The array is designed to comprise 32 telescopes with 6-meter apertures within LHAASO at an altitude of approximately 4410 meters. Each camera contains 1616 silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). We developed a front-end readout electronics (FEE) board integrating 16 channels of SiPM gain compensation and high-speed waveform sampling for operation at high altitude and over a wide temperature range. The gain compensation circuit independently adjusts the operating voltage of each SiPM according to its temperature and monitors the actual operating voltage. Previous tests of the adopted compensation scheme showed SiPM gain drift below 2% from -20 to 30 degrees Celsius. The waveform sampling circuit uses two 14-bit AC9628 analog-to-digital converters, each operating in eight-channel mode, to digitize the SiPM pulse waveform at 250 million samples per second. The integral nonlinearity of the DC response is 0.0709% over a differential DC voltage range of -950 mV to +950 mV at the AC9628 input. Equivalent electrical pulses with a full width at half maximum of 37.42 ns are used to simulate the SiPM output signals. At a differential pulse amplitude of approximately 237 mV at the AC9628 input, the pulse integral area resolution is 0.2725%. This paper presents the circuit design and performance tests of the FEE for the LACT camera.

papers.title: Geodesic-informed neural networks for testing spacetimes with S2
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits around Sagittarius A*, in particular that of S2, test the spacetime of the Galactic Center. Such analyses usually integrate the equations of motion for every likelihood evaluation and sample the posterior. We develop a differentiable orbit model for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes that obtains the parameters, their uncertainties and the Bayesian evidence by optimization rather than sampling. In the Geodesic-Informed Neural Network (GINN), the conserved quantities, the shape of the orbit and the redshift are computed exactly from the metric, and a neural network constrained by the geodesic equation represents the time evolution of the radial phase. The physical parameters and the network weights minimize a single loss with Adam and Gauss-Newton steps, and the curvature at the minimum gives the uncertainties and the evidence. We test this Gaussian approximation against a second-order expansion and an exact geodesic solver, and apply GINN to the S2 data in the Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, hairy Horndeski, Bardeen, Janis-Newman-Winicour and Yukawa spacetimes. GINN reproduces the estimates and uncertainties of the exact solver. For Schwarzschild we find $M=(4.32\pm0.22)\times10^6\,M_\odot$ and $D=8.33\pm0.21$ kpc. No spacetime deviates significantly from Schwarzschild; a Yukawa correction, for example, is limited to $|\delta|<0.011$ (95%) at a range of about 180 AU. No additional parameter improves the fit enough to pay its Occam penalty, so the Bayes factors range from inconclusive to moderate in favor of Schwarzschild. The Gaussian approximation is accurate when the hair enters the metric linearly and conservative when it enters only through its square. When the posterior is close to Gaussian, GINN gives the estimates, their uncertainties and the evidence from a single optimization, and the same derivatives quantify departures from it.

papers.title: Asgard/NOTT: L-band nulling interferometry at the VLTI IV. Prospects for characterising hot exozodiacal dust
papers.abstract: Near-infrared interferometric surveys have revealed extended emission around the photosphere of $\approx 40$ main-sequence stars, attributed to the presence of hot exozodiacal dust (HEZD). A promising technique for investigating this phenomenon is nulling interferometry. The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) nulling interferometer NOTT (Nulling Observations of exoplaneTs and dusT) is designed to characterise exoplanets and HEZD in the $L'$ band ($3.5-4.0\,\mu$m). We aim to assess NOTT's potential for the detection and characterisation of HEZD with various instrumental and model parameter configurations. We model the HEZD as an optically thin dust ring, using the nearby Sun-like star $\tau$ Ceti with HEZD as a reference model. Applying the end-to-end nulling tool SCIFYsim to model the instrumental response of NOTT to simulated HEZD brightness distributions, we evaluate how variations in HEZD and instrumental parameters affect NOTT's key observables: the photon flux rate and the null depth. We demonstrate that NOTT is capable of disentangling stellar and dust contributions to the signal and detecting HEZD. The null depth and photon flux rate are sensitive to the HEZD geometry, with inclination, position angle, and ring location having the strongest impact on the signal. Although the detailed temporal signatures are target-specific, the results can be generalised to other systems. NOTT has the potential to deliver unprecedented sensitivity for HEZD observations, granting access to detailed information through spectral dispersion, beam-combination schemes, and exploitation of sky rotation. This enables more sensitive HEZD detections than is possible with current instruments, and improved spatial constraints on the dust, as well as variability studies.

papers.title: LEMUR: A Searchable Web Archive of Deep Chandra Images of Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present LEMUR, a publicly accessible archive of uniformly reduced, deep Chandra images of 2,569 galaxies and galaxy clusters (including groups), comprising 5,505 ACIS observations and 138.8 Ms of exposure. By combining the publicly available imaging observations of each target, we provide background-subtracted, exposure-corrected images in broad, soft, and hard bands at the native ACIS pixel scale of 0.492 arcsec. Our primary goal is to make the wealth of archival Chandra observations accessible to researchers without requiring specialized expertise in X-ray data reduction. Each observation is reprocessed with CIAO, filtered for background flares, and reduced with settings chosen to preserve faint diffuse emission; the merged images are exposure corrected and background subtracted using the ACIS blank-sky backgrounds in a broad (0.5-7.0 keV), a soft (0.5-2.0 keV), and a hard (2.0-7.0 keV) band. For every object, we measure an X-ray center at the peak of its diffuse emission, and we provide a morphological similarity search based on embeddings from the AstroCLIP foundation model, in which nearest neighbors share cool-core status in 73% of matched cluster pairs, compared with 51% by chance. Photometry of 275 point sources agrees with the Chandra Source Catalog to within 3% in the broad band. The images, along with their counts images, background models, exposure maps, and quick-look stamps, are available through a searchable web archive at https://lemur-archive.lemur-xray.workers.dev/. The catalog tables are archived on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24351915), and all code is open source at https://github.com/crhea93/Lemur.

papers.title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We train a spherical graph convolutional network to infer the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ directly from multifrequency cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode maps on the cut sky. We test the network on simulations of a generic ground-based experiment including lensed CMB, inhomogeneous noise, and stochastic Galactic dust and synchrotron emission. We compare the network with a multifrequency bandpower likelihood built from the same 20,000 simulations used to train it. Working directly on the maps, with no power-spectrum estimation or component separation, the network reduces the root-mean-square error on $r$ by a factor of 1.3 and gives well-calibrated 68% intervals 1.2 times narrower than the likelihood with the same prior. Saliency maps show that the network learns to favor the deepest regions of the sky and the cleanest frequency channels without being given the survey depth. Both approaches are tied to the foreground model they are built on: the network generalizes to some alternative foreground models without retraining, but not to a three-dimensional dust model with line-of-sight variations. The network can be extended to marginalize over foreground models by training on a broad family, making direct map-level neural inference a promising route to $r$ for future $B$-mode analyses.

papers.title: Stars and gas in the most metal-poor galaxies -- II. Search for VMS and determination of stellar population and nebular properties at $Z\lesssim0.1\,Z_\odot$
papers.abstract: Constraining the properties of OB-star populations and ionized gas at low metallicity is essential for understanding a broad range of astrophysical objects, from stellar black holes to the first galaxies. Rest-frame UV spectra of nearby metal-poor galaxies provide crucial constraints on theoretical predictions of low-metallicity stars and gas. However, such spectra are scarce at $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, and candidate Very Massive Stars (VMS) remain elusive. We analyse optical and new UV spectra of nearby star-forming galaxies with $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, selected for their nebular He II $\lambda4686$ emission and lack of Wolf-Rayet blue and red bumps, making them promising targets for VMS searches. Some galaxies exhibit stellar wind features (group 1), while others do not (group 2). For group 1, we compare STARBURST99, GALAXEV, and BPASS predictions with observed stellar lines to constrain OB-population ages and masses. The inferred ages are too old for VMS to be present. We also use pySTARBURST99 and GALAXEV photoionization models to investigate the ionized gas in a subsample, finding no evidence for VMS-dominated ionization. The absence of detected VMS may reflect their rarity, our limited sample size, or shortcomings in current models. Moreover, reproducing the extreme optical and UV line ratios simultaneously requires unrealistic N/O, ionization parameters, or Lyman continuum escape fractions, suggesting that multiple ionizing-source populations may be needed.

papers.title: WFST0533buha (Bi'an): A Fast Blue Ultraluminous Transient Candidate with Unusual Blue/NUV Colors
papers.abstract: We present WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT) candidate discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope Deep High-cadence $ugr$-band Survey. The source brightened by approximately 2.5 mag in $u$ within 3 days and has a half-maximum timescale ($t_{1/2}$) shorter than 6 days. Two spectra show a blue, featureless continuum but do not provide a secure redshift. Einstein Probe observations yield only X-ray upper limits, while a faint radio counterpart was detected at 15 GHz with the VLA. The early $u$-band detection and intensive multiband coverage of Bi'an demonstrate the value of deep, high-cadence blue-band observations for discovering and characterizing FBUTs at early phases. Notably, Bi'an shows redder blue/NUV colors than AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting possible diversity in the short-wavelength properties of FBUTs.

papers.title: The infrared arc around $\alpha$ Crucis: a weak interaction with a structured interstellar medium
papers.abstract: Infrared arc-shaped structures around early-type stars are commonly interpreted as stellar wind bow shocks, although their morphology may also be shaped by gas motions and density variations in the surrounding interstellar medium. We present a multiwavelength study of the infrared arc associated with the nearby $\alpha$ Crucis system, comprising HD 108248 (B0.5 IV), HD 108249 (B1 V), and HD 108250 (B4 V). We combine WISE, Herschel, Planck, stellar astrometry, and eROSITA X-ray data to investigate the structure and its relation to the stellar components. The WISE W4 ridge extends over $\sim$0.65 pc and has a median PSF-corrected width of $\sim$0.037 pc. The HD 108248/HD 108249 pair lies $\sim$0.13 pc from the ridge, compared with $\sim$0.17 pc for HD 108250. Relative to the mean motion of the Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) subgroup of the Scorpius-Centaurus association, the close pair is consistent with LCC, whereas HD 108250 has a transverse peculiar velocity of only $\sim$1.8 km s$^{-1}$. Its motion lies within $\sim$23$^\circ$ of the geometrical symmetry axis of the infrared arc, but points in the opposite sense from the arc. Herschel maps show slightly higher median dust temperature ($\Delta T_d\sim$0.8 K) and molecular-hydrogen column density ($\Delta N_{\rm H2}\sim$7$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$) toward the W4-defined region than in the nearby background. On larger scales, Planck maps reveal a strongly structured microwave environment around the system. Both the HD 108248/HD 108249 pair and HD 108250 are detected by eROSITA, with the former approximately 60 times more luminous in X-rays. The combined morphology, kinematics, and dust properties do not support an unambiguous classical high-velocity bow-shock interpretation. Instead, the arc likely traces a weak interaction between the multiple stellar system and an inhomogeneous ambient medium.

papers.title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
papers.abstract: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.
